action: Title card and agenda slides open the retopology chapter; no Blender yet.
why: Sets the chapter agenda: what retopology is, then terms.

action: Slide lists real-time game topology needs: low polygon count, fast to process, more geometry where it matters.
why: Contrasts game topology with the offline route this course takes.

action: Slide for animation and offline rendering: mesh gets subdivided at render, higher count is fine, mostly quads.
why: Justifies a moderate quad count and a Subdivision modifier.

action: Slide on why retopology exists (cut sculpt polygon count, deformable loops); the artist then alt-tabs to Blender showing the sculpt.
why: Goal statement: animation-ready mesh from a multi-million-face sculpt.

action: Recap slide of the why-list, then a blank terminology heading slide.
why: Bridge to terminology.

action: In Edit Mode on three small demo planes (triangle-ish, quad, n-gon) the artist selects one edge and extrudes it with E to grow a strip of quads, with the statistics overlay on.
view: perspective, Edit Mode, Statistics overlay on
why: Shows that quads give clean strips while tris and n-gons stop edge flow.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.extrude_edge_only on an edge list (see extrude_border in the helpers)

action: Slide defines poles: 3 edges is a 3-pole, 5 a 5-pole, 6 a 6-pole.
why: Introduces valence vocabulary.

action: On a flat quad grid the artist loop-cuts and slides to show a 3-pole/5-pole pair redirecting an edge loop; slide ends repeat the idea of redirecting flow.
view: top-down perspective, Edit Mode, vertex select
why: Demonstrates how a pole turns or stops a loop.
reader_equivalent: census(obj) counts valence 3 and 5 as allowed poles

action: Finished example head in rotating perspective with the rig visible: loops round eyes, mouth, nose and ear on the already retopologized mesh.
why: Shows the target: loops round the ear so it can be deformed.

action: Slide lists the face loop sets (eyes, nose, mouth, nasolabial, face contour, ear) then a chapter title card.
why: Names the five loop sets built next.

action: Object Mode orthographic front, whole character with clothes; the Outliner shows nothing named yet (default Collection full of Cube, Roundcube names).
view: front orthographic with split view, matcap gray
why: Starting state before organising for retopology.

action: Drags clothes and hair into a Highpoly collection (tooltip: Ctrl to link), then hides clothes and hair, leaving the nude body.
why: Separates sculpts from the low-poly meshes that will be made.

action: Drags the Solidify thickness on the skirt (Shift held for fine steps) while the camera orbits close to the hem.
why: Fixes shell thickness after rescaling the scene.

action: Checks the clothes' Mirror modifiers (axis X, Clipping, merge 0.001 m) then hides clothes and hair and moves the arm sculpt with G.
why: Tidy-up before applying modifiers and fusing the body.

action: In Sculpt Mode with Grab active, opens the Remesh popover (Voxel Size field about 0.013 m, Preserve Volume and Attributes on) and then drags the voxel size interactively with R, a reference grid showing 0.0059 m.
view: perspective, Sculpt Mode, wireframe on sculpt
why: Choosing a voxel size small enough to keep ear and eyelid detail.

action: Remesh result judged too coarse or soft; undoes, then reopens the interactive voxel size, the box reading 0.00164 m, and states the first value lost the detail.
why: Trial and error: pick voxel size by whether the nostril and lip detail survive.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_remesh with a smaller voxel_size, then mesh_report

action: Adds volume to the lips with Clay Strips, then switches to Crease Polish to re-cut the lip line; brush radius changes with F between strokes.
view: front close-up on mouth, Sculpt Mode
why: Hard lip and lid lines give the later vertices something to follow.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes brush='crease' along the lip line; radius about 0.1 of mouth width

action: Leaves Sculpt Mode with the Ctrl+Tab pie, enters local view with /, then renames objects with F2 (hands and similar).
tool: Mode pie (Ctrl+Tab), Local View, F2 rename
why: Housekeeping before joining hands and feet onto the body.

action: Adds ankle bones with Clay Strips in a clipped side view, rotating around the ankle; inner bone placed higher than the outer.
why: Ankle landmarks are re-cut so loops can follow them.
reader_equivalent: sculpt_strokes brush='clay_strips' two small dabs, inner at higher Z than outer

action: Deletes the now-unneeded hands and feet objects (X), renames the remaining pieces, and keeps a Mirror modifier with Mirror Object set to body.
why: Only the fused body, brows, eyes remain for retopology.

action: Renames the leftover meshes (body, brows, eyes) in the Outliner and selects the Scene Collection to add a new collection.
why: Names things before the topology pass.

action: Creates a new empty collection with C in the Outliner and types Lowpoly for it.
why: All retopology meshes will live here.

action: Adds a plane with Shift+A in the Lowpoly collection, drops it in front of the face, hides brows and lashes, snaps the cursor.
why: The plane is the seed that becomes all face loops.

action: Enters Edit Mode on the plane, turns snapping on (face project with rotate and scale) and moves the plane onto the lid with G while Alt is held.
tool: Edit Mode, Snap to Face Project, G
view: perspective, close on right eye, Edit Mode
why: Placing the first ring on the lid edge.
reader_equivalent: ellipse(...) dropped with Surf.drop onto the sculpt

action: Starts with a small ring round the eye and extrudes it twice with E then S, scaling each ring out, then nudges vertices with G; statistics show 24 vertices and 16 faces.
why: Three rings of 8 around the lid.

action: Retopology overlay is on, so the faces show blue; select all, Shift+N to recalculate normals when they look dark.
why: Blue faces confirm normals face the viewer.

action: Duplicates a vertex and extrudes outward to build the nasolabial line from nose side to mouth corner and chin, then opens Add Modifier search and types mirror.
why: A mirror is needed because the artist cannot tell where the face midline is.

action: With the Mirror on (Clipping, merge 0.001 m) places the mouth loop and nasolabial line, using G and S often with Alt held for surface snapping; stats read about 65 edges.
why: Loops run through the centre line without gaps.
reader_equivalent: half=True rings pinned to x=0 under Mirror use_clip

action: Rings are placed round the nose and the mouth (about 40 faces now) and selected; L selects linked, Shift+N recalculates normals.
view: close-up nose and mouth, Edit Mode
why: Both rings must be quad rings of the same count before joining.

action: Builds the ear loop and the face contour in side views, Ctrl-click extruding vertices, recalculating normals and moving rows with G a few vertices at a time.
why: Ear base ring and the jaw contour frame the face mask.
reader_equivalent: Surf.ring on the ear base with n=8, closed

action: Rotates around all five loop sets (112 vertices, 56 faces), then starts filling gaps at the bottom of the mouth: selects two edges and presses F.
why: Order starts at the mouth and works outward.

action: Keeps pressing F between edges; when F makes nothing, opens Preferences > Get Extensions and checks that F2 is installed (list also shows Auto Mirror, LoopTools, Screencast Keys).

settings.installed: Auto Mirror, F2, LoopTools, Screencast Keys

why: F2 lets F make a face from a vertex or edge.

action: Most of the face is now filled (151 vertices, 111 faces); a few places still need extra loop cuts.
why: Fill by quads only; triangles are avoided by adding cuts.

action: Adds two Ctrl+R loop cuts (orange preview) at the forehead and temple so the face border follows the sculpt; statistics climb to 185 vertices, 143 faces.
why: Mismatched counts are fixed by a loop cut, not a triangle.

action: Adds a Shrinkwrap modifier below the Mirror: Nearest Surface Point, On Surface, target body, offset 0 m, with On Cage on, so the cage sticks to the sculpt.
why: Keeps new loops on the surface while the artist edits.
reader_equivalent: shrinkwrap block in step 7; snap(obj, S)

action: Leaves Edit Mode with the Ctrl+Tab pie into Sculpt Mode on the low-poly plane to smooth it; Grab brush is current (Size 396 px, Strength 0.400).
why: Smoothing is done in Sculpt Mode on the cage.

action: Sculpt Mode on the cage: Relax Slide brush with Shift held, radius changed with F many times, short strokes over cheek and jaw; Object properties show Wireframe on. Then Tab to Edit Mode and extrudes the mouth ring inward with E then Z.
why: Evens quad spacing while keeping vertices on the surface.

action: Moves lip vertices with G, uses Alt+Z for x-ray, and Ctrl+R with 2 cuts across the lip edge loops; snapped to the sculpt.
why: More rows on the lip so it can open and purse.

action: At the nostril, selects the ring and scales it in twice with E then S, even edge count noted aloud before the fill.
why: Prepares an even ring for Grid Fill.

action: Opens the Face menu (Ctrl+F) to Grid Fill the nostril ring; with an odd count Blender shows an error, so the artist undoes four times and cuts again.
why: Grid Fill needs an even count.
reader_equivalent: cap(obj, point, span=2) raises if the border count is odd

action: Relax Slide in Sculpt Mode with Shift held, radius cycled by F (about 184 to 316 px), many overlapping strokes over cheeks, chin and forehead.
view: front and side perspective, wireframe visible
why: Evens out quads after fills.

action: Relax Slide at the top of the head, then switches to Grab (Size about 326 px, Strength 0.400) to push the forehead cage back onto the sculpt.
why: Corrects where the cage sits above or inside the sculpt.

action: At the back of the head, extrudes edges behind the ear to the centre line with G, then Ctrl+R with 7 cuts, yellow preview strips across the skull.
why: Back of the head filled with evenly spaced rows.
reader_equivalent: Surf.ring half rows up the skull

action: Fills the back and crown row by row with F, adding Ctrl+R cuts (2) at the top where faces would otherwise be uneven.
why: Completes the skull.

action: Adds a Ctrl+R loop cut round the ear (yellow preview) to give extra geometry behind the ear, shrinkwrap on.
why: More faces round the ear base.
reader_equivalent: extra ring around the ear base

action: Relax Slide with Shift on the geometry round the ear and cheek, radius varied between about 218 and 340 px; stats now 891 vertices, 840 faces.
why: Even out after ear fill.

action: At the neck, selects the lower border and extrudes it straight down with G, turns Clipping back on, then relaxes the neck with Relax Slide (392 px, strength 1.0); 1,005 vertices.
why: Neck rows are cut to match the torso later.

action: Applies the Mirror then relaxes the whole head with Shift held (Size 166 to 334 px, Strength 1.0); 1,933 vertices, 1,896 faces.
why: Smooth without the mirror pulling the centre.

action: In Edit Mode opens the N-panel Edit tab, where Auto Mirror shows axis X, Positive, Threshold 0.00, Cut and Mirror and Use Clip on.
why: Re-adds the Mirror modifier after smoothing.
reader_equivalent: Mirror modifier with use_clip and merge 0.001

action: Searches Preferences for Auto Mirror, then clicks AutoMirror, which deletes the -X half in the selection and adds a Mirror modifier; the middle edge ring highlights.
why: Brings back symmetry cleanly.

action: Deletes annotation lines; then a summary slide lists the chapter outcome.
why: Closes the face chapter.

action: Closing and next-chapter title cards; nothing on screen to study.
why: Transition.

action: Finished rigged body in pose mode: dense loops at the hip, thigh, knee preserve volume as the leg moves.
view: wireframe overlay, front and three-quarter perspective
why: Shows what loops are for before building them.

action: Lowpoly collection selected; the high-poly sculpt is on screen (about 3.2 million vertices and faces by the statistics overlay) with the small face cage on top; says the next thing to add is a circle.
why: Starting the body with the face already done.

action: Adds a circle with Shift+A > Mesh > Circle in the Lowpoly collection and, in the Add Circle redo panel, changes Vertices from 32 to 10 (radius about 1 m, Fill Type Nothing).
why: A 10-vertex ring is the seed for the torso and arm circles.
reader_equivalent: add_grid(low, rings of n points, closed=True)

action: In Edit Mode selects two edges and presses F to bridge them, repeating with F and G while moving verts with snapping (Alt) so that the shoulder patch fills without triangles; stats 54 vertices, 33-34 faces.
view: side perspective of shoulder, Edit Mode
why: Building the shoulder loop patch by hand with quads only.

action: Ctrl+R repeatedly to subdivide the arm loops (skipping one), checking the arm ring: with the right count the select-count shows 20 vertices; shoulder loop runs to the front and back centre.
view: shoulder close-up, Edit Mode, Mirror and Shrinkwrap on
why: Arm ring of 20 matches what the rest of the body needs.

action: Moves the lower neck border vertices with G; selecting the ring shows 9 vertices and 8 edges, meaning half of it; the head's neck border must match; Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode shows head and body cages together.
view: front perspective, Edit Mode then Object Mode
why: Neck border counts must be equal before joining.

action: Relax Slide with Alt held (Size 268 px, Strength 1.000) over the shoulder and upper chest wireframe to even the quads; mentions the head and body will be merged and double edge loops smoothed.
view: shoulder and upper back, Sculpt Mode
why: Cage follows the sculpt shape before breasts and ribs.

action: Chest: concentric rings round each breast, grid filled inside; turns off snapping before extruding the rib band down with G; stats 418 vertices, 382 faces then 800 edges.
why: Rings follow the breast form; snapping would collapse the extrusion.

action: Relax Slide with Shift (Size 372/292/290 px, Strength 1.000) over the abdomen; then Tab to Edit Mode with a row of faces selected in orange.
why: Even rows on the waist.

action: Selects the rib edge loop and bevels with Ctrl+B; in the Bevel redo panel raises Segments to 2 (Width about 0.0057 m, Offset type, Profile 0.5, Loop Slide on) to add two loops where the rib line is.
why: Extra loops where the sculpt has a ridge.

action: Extrudes the hip band with G, adds Ctrl+R cuts (2) and moves them with G and Shift to follow the buttock and hip crease, Shrinkwrap on.
view: rear and front three-quarter, Edit Mode
why: Hip loops follow the crease for later bending.
reader_equivalent: strip under the crotch in [hips-leg] block

action: Rear view: Relax Slide with Shift (Size 260 to 412 px, Strength 1.000) over the buttock and thighs, F resizing between strokes, then pulls back to the whole back to check flow.
why: Evens quads at the hip and thigh.

action: Adds a Ctrl+R loop cut at the elbow, scales it with S and moves with G (Shift for fine), checking the arm silhouette from the side; arm ring selected reads 20 vertices.
tool: Loop Cut and Slide, S, G
view: side perspective of arm, Edit Mode
why: Elbow ring sits at the bend.

action: Relax Slide on the arm (Size 202 to 324 px, Strength 1.000), with Shift or Alt held, brush size cycled with F; checks the cage follows the sculpt.
why: Arm rings follow the sculpt.

action: Relaxes the elbow, then Tab into Edit Mode with Ctrl+Alt (x-ray) at the elbow where the dent is, getting ready to cut joint loops (1,852 vertices, 1,793 faces).
why: Joint patch goes on the back of the elbow.

action: At the knee: Relax Slide with Shift (Size 292 to 336 px, Strength 1.000), F resizing a dozen times, so the knee loops sit on the front of the knee and the rows run straight.
view: front and side of knee, Sculpt Mode
why: Knee patch must keep its point when bent.

action: Rotates round the whole body with Alt held, relaxing the legs and arms; body is done at 1,874 vertices and 1,815 faces, hands next.
why: Overall check before hands.

action: Moves the thumb cube into place on the sculpt with many G moves (Shift held), snapping to the surface; the other four fingers already sit side by side. Stats: 200 vertices, 170 faces.
why: Thumb is a finger with one joint less.
reader_equivalent: S.ring rows along the finger with closed=True

action: Selects a finger and checks it has two faces across the top and three down each side; ten vertices round at the joint.
why: Gives a 10-vertex ring per finger.

action: Scales the knuckle edge row with S then Y, moves with G then Y; opens right-click > LoopTools > Relax on the selected row; stats 34 vertices.
why: Evens the finger-root loop.

action: Selects the ring round all finger roots (34 vertices) with GG slide, extrudes it back toward the wrist, and states the ring is 34 against the forearm's 20.
why: Counts must reduce from 34 to 20 before bridging.
reader_equivalent: no one-call helper; joint_patch run lengthwise to change counts

action: Relaxes the back of the hand with Shift (Relax Slide Size 204 px, Strength 1.000), then in Edit Mode selects a palm loop with 26 vertices, notes it, duplicates and applies the Shrinkwrap on a copy (message: applied modifier was not first) before reducing the count.
tool: Relax Slide, Apply modifier on copy
view: back and palm of hand, Edit Mode
why: Count reduction from 26 toward 20 needs the cage settled on the surface.

action: After two more vertices are removed the wrist ring reads 20, matching the forearm's 20; hand cage is then viewed from several angles in Edit Mode.
view: back of hand and palm, Edit Mode
why: Equal counts make Bridge Edge Loops possible.
reader_equivalent: bridge_near(low, wrist_point) needs equal border edge counts

action: Thumb finished; relaxes the thumb with Relax Slide (Size 248 px, Strength 1.000), then selects fingertips from above to finish them; 1,022 vertices, 1,011 faces.
why: Fingertips come next.

action: On a fingertip selects a face patch, insets it (I) and moves points with G many times (x5 to x10) so the cap forms a small rounded grid where a nail would sit; says nails would use the same steps.
why: Adds support loops at the tip.

action: Both hands finished: Object Mode, selects the hand cube, Ctrl+Tab and Shift+Alt orbits to check; the hand shows as one orange-outlined mesh (1,172 vertices, 1,161 faces, a hand and forearm).
why: Final look before joining to the body.

action: Selects the plane, Ctrl+J to join (they share the same modifiers), then in Edit Mode selects the wrist edge loops on both pieces and uses Ctrl+E > Bridge Edge Loops; the two 20-vertex rings connect.
why: Hand attaches to the forearm without triangles.

action: Moves on to feet: Relax Slide with Alt held, then Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode, isolates the leg and foot view, and Shift+A > Mesh to add a new Cube as the toe seed.
view: front and rear perspective, Object Mode
why: Feet follow the same cube-per-toe method.

action: Foot cage built and relaxed (Size 382 px, Strength 1.000); Tab to Edit Mode where the ankle border selected reads 26 vertices against the leg's count, so the ankle ring needs reducing (26, 24, 22).
view: heel and ankle perspective, Edit Mode
why: Compare ring counts before bridging foot to leg.

action: Relax Slide with Shift over the legs, then torso and arms, then a front view of the whole body (Size 216 to 374 px, Strength 1.000); 4,969 vertices, 4,885 faces.
why: Smooth the whole body after joins.

action: Relaxes legs and rear view; the full body in Object Mode reports 9,953 vertices and 9,924 faces (about 10,000) on the low-poly. Then the artist says the next step is eye sockets and mouth.
view: rear and front perspective, Sculpt/Object Mode
why: Confirms the body is complete at about 10,000 faces.

action: Opens the Mesh Edit Mode overlays popover to turn the Retopology overlay off, then moves the upper lip row up and the lower row down with G then Z, alternating, to open the mouth slit; lip vertices at 5,388 vertices total.
view: close-up of mouth, Edit Mode, wireframe off
why: Opens the lip border so a mouth bag can be extruded.

action: Result viewed in Object Mode: the whole low-poly head and body with eye cavities and mouth cavity added, shaded smooth with Shift+Q Z; statistics 10,449 vertices, 10,422 faces.
why: Confirms the finished body count.

action: With Eye - Stylized and Jaw - Stylized in the Lowpoly collection, scales the eyeball into the socket from the right orthographic view (scale X reading 0.98), hides the original sculpt eye, shades smooth through the Object context menu, orbits to check the eye turns inside the lid.
view: right orthographic then perspective, Object Mode
why: Eyeball must fit the socket and rotate without poking through.
reader_equivalent: obj.scale, obj.location, rotation_euler test of 30 degrees

action: Selects the low-poly, turns Shrinkwrap back on, picks the vertex group no shrinkwrap in its field and inverts it; patches of the sculpt show through the face before the group is applied; x-ray shows the sockets and mouth bag.
view: front and side view, Object Mode, X-ray on
why: Keeps socket and mouth bag vertices from snapping onto the skin.

action: Adds a Multires modifier via Add Modifier search (typed mu), moves it above the Shrinkwrap in the stack; Levels still 0.
why: Detail will be carried by Multires before the shrinkwrap is applied.

action: Multires levels now show viewport 2, sculpt 2, render 2 (174,880 vertices, 174,440 faces on the stats); opens the Shrinkwrap dropdown and chooses Apply, hovering the tooltip that says apply modifier and remove from the stack.
why: The sculpt's shape is pulled onto the subdivided cage.

action: In Sculpt Mode on the Multires low-poly, uses Crease Polish (Size about 92 to 104 px, Strength 0.250) to mark palm lines, F to resize, Shift+Q to switch brush; then Ctrl+Tab back to Object Mode. Stats 375,192 vertices, 166,752 faces.
why: Re-marks detail that the shrinkwrap softened.
reader_equivalent: no equivalent on Multires levels; do this on the sculpt before reprojection (Gap)

action: Final modifier is Subdivision, Catmull-Clark, Levels viewport 1, render 2; the artist rotates the body to confirm the sculpt details carried over.
why: Light render-time subdivision replaces the Multires.

action: Chapter outro cards then the next chapter title card.
why: Transition.

action: Chapter 9 intro: layout workspace with a finished rigged character and clothes (shirt, shorts), Pose Mode deformation test; the modifier stack has Mirror, Solidify, Subdivision and Armature on the garment.
why: Shows why garment loops must match the body's.

action: In a fresh scene with the finished body (named body.001) and clothes sculpts, renames eye and jaw objects, sets up a clothes retopology collection and tidies names; object count 24, stats about 961,000 vertices.
why: Prepares a clean scene for the garment pass.

action: Opens a Text Editor panel on the right listing the six cloth steps (base topology from the body, align with seams, align with folds, reinforce seams, add thickness, reproject sculpted details) and keeps it docked while working.
view: close-up of collar, Object Mode, text editor split
why: Artist keeps a checklist on screen; the six steps match Order of work 19 to 24.

action: In Edit Mode on shirt_retopo (copied from the body cage) moves hem vertices with G and Alt snapping so the bottom edge follows the shirt; Mirror (clipping off) and Shrinkwrap (target Cube.001, Nearest Surface Point, On Surface, offset 0) show in the stack.
view: close-up of hem, Edit Mode; video at 4.5x speed
why: Hem and body-copy faces are re-seated on the garment.

action: Base shirt topology after cutting the body copy: about 420 vertices and 376 faces; fixes sleeve armhole with Shift-fine G moves and Edge Slide, then deselects and checks the whole shirt before moving on.
why: Base topology is ready for the seam step.

action: Slides the sleeve-end loops with G and Alt, flagging with a note that a loop at the back is not needed; sleeve opening shows quad rows following the garment hem.
view: back-side view of sleeve, Edit Mode
why: Slide existing loops onto sculpted seams; remove unneeded ones.

action: Orbits the shirt as the seams (neck, sleeves, hem) now sit on the sculpted seam lines, a 'applied modifier was not first' warning visible after a duplicate-and-apply shrinkwrap; vertices 479, faces 434.
why: Check that seams are aligned from all sides.

action: Cleans away annotation lines and adjusts the hem loops with G x2 and G x4 (Alt held); the bottom hem now sits flush with the sculpt; 511 vertices, 464 faces.
why: Finishing seam alignment before folds.

action: Moves selected loops outward and places new loops on the folds of the sleeve (G, Ctrl+R with 2 cuts, Alt); vertices 589, faces 540; the sleeve cage follows each fold ridge.
view: close-up of sleeve fold, Edit Mode
why: Loops follow fold ridges so subdivision keeps them.
reader_equivalent: joint_patch lengthwise on the fold edges

action: Whole shirt viewed from front and sides after folds are aligned; vertices 587, faces 538; Text Editor with the six steps is raised to move to step 4.
why: Confirms folds are done.

action: Ctrl+Z three times to undo, checks Auto Merge Vertices tooltip is on, then selects the seam loop (Ctrl+click) and bevels it with Ctrl+B and Shift for fine width: Offset 0.0017 m, Segments 2, Profile 0.5; where two seams cross a small patch appears.
view: close-up of sleeve seam, Edit Mode
why: Seam loop becomes three loops to stay crisp when subdivided.

action: In Object Mode adds a temporary Subdivision modifier to judge the shirt thickness, drags Solidify thickness with Shift for fine control and types 0.007; Solidify Mode Simple, Offset -1.0, Rim Fill on; shrinkwrap is above it with target Cube.001.
view: close-up of sleeve opening, Object Mode
why: Thickness is gauged on a subdivided view, then Subdivision is removed.

action: Removes the Subdivision, applies Solidify while the Shrinkwrap is still above it; stats 2,538 vertices, 2,542 faces; the result collapses: Blender warns 'applied modifier was not first' and the shell sticks to the sculpt.
view: front and local view, Object Mode
why: Shows why the shrinkwrap must skip the inner shell (next).

action: Explains the problem on screen: inner shell and rim are also shrinkwrapped, so everything lands on the outer surface; artist undoes twice (Ctrl+Z x2) to retry.
view: close-up of sleeve cuff, Object Mode
why: Motivates the shell and rim vertex groups.

action: After setting the Solidify output vertex groups, makes a combined group and picks it in the Shrinkwrap vertex group field with the invert button on, so only the outer face snaps; isolated shirt now shows correct thickness.
view: local view with Shift+Alt orbit, Object then Edit Mode
why: Outer shell snaps, inner shell and rim stay put.

action: Rounds the rim: selects the rim loop and presses Alt+S to scale along the normals (the header reads about 0.0014 m), Ctrl+R cut with 1 cut; vertices 2,582 and faces 2,584 before, 2,610 after.
view: close-up of neck opening, Edit Mode
why: Rounded rim so the cuff edge is not flat.
reader_equivalent: bmesh.ops.shrink_fatten / move rim verts along normal

action: Back in Object Mode removes the inner faces nobody will see (collar and sleeves hollow); the shirt reads as a thick garment from outside with a visible neck opening; Text Editor steps panel is shown again.
why: Finish of step 5.

action: Adds Multires above the Shrinkwrap and subdivides to level 2 (shirt: 27,050 vertices, 26,848 faces), says to subdivide once more; opens the Shrinkwrap menu and applies it; no Apply Base on clothes.
why: The sculpt's folds are carried by the Multires which stays for baking.
reader_equivalent: [cloth] block: multires_subdivide x2 then modifier_apply Shrinkwrap

action: Unhides the whole scene, hides the shirt and starts on the skirt; the Multires on the shirt is at level 2; Alt+H reveals hidden objects, body retopo and eyes shown.
why: Next garment: the skirt.

action: Skirt: Edit Mode on skirt_retopo with Mirror (clip on, 0.001 m) and Shrinkwrap targeting Circle.002 (the skirt sculpt, Nearest Surface Point, On Surface, offset 0); moves pleat-edge vertices with G (some with Shift) to sit on the folds; 117 vertices, 90 faces.
why: Loops sit on the pleat edges.
reader_equivalent: extrude rings by bmesh and snap(skirt, Sc)

action: Creates a face with F on a pleat corner where the pleat opens, and decides to leave a gap open until later cuts allow a quad (121 to 117 vertices; 90 to 91 faces).
view: close-up of skirt pleat, Edit Mode
why: Avoid triangles: leave the hole open rather than force it.
reader_equivalent: cap() raises if the border is odd

action: Skirt after Solidify: in Edit Mode adds a Ctrl+R loop (Cuts 1), selects faces on the inner hem and deletes them with X, then removes more inner faces higher up so the inside of the skirt keeps only what can be seen; Shrinkwrap target Circle.002 with inverted Group.
view: low and underside views of the skirt hem, Edit Mode
why: The inside of a skirt can be seen, so inner faces are kept higher than on the shirt.

action: Adds Multires above the Shrinkwrap, clicks Subdivide once (Levels Viewport 1, Sculpt 1, Render 1 after Delete Higher), tooltip warns Delete Higher loses detail.
view: front perspective of skirt, Object Mode
why: Skirt takes only one level, since its sculpt has little fine detail.

action: Boots: duplicates the body's foot and shin topology into shoe_retopo, turns snapping on, and moves the rows by G (6x speed) to sit on the boot; Shrinkwrap target Cube.004; verts 573, faces 538.
view: side and front perspective of boot, Edit Mode, video at 6x
why: Boot base comes from the body's foot, then slides onto boot seams.
reader_equivalent: copy body_retopo, delete faces, snap(shoe, Sc)

action: Finishes the extra boot pieces: Ctrl+Tab to Object Mode, Alt+H to reveal hidden objects, clears the viewport mask; the object (strap and ring) already has a Mirror, Subdivision and Solidify stack.
view: front perspective and close-up of boot strap, Object Mode
why: Modelled pieces are carried over, not retopologized.
reader_equivalent: duplicate and apply modifiers, remove unneeded loops

action: Strap: Ctrl+M mirrors on X then Return; G moves duplicated piece, X deletes; before mirroring, Ctrl+Z, makes sure Auto Merge is off, then Shift+D duplicates again; strap sits at the boot's outer side; stats 384 vertices.
